Oando Plc has announced plans to raise N203.8bn through a rights issue to strengthen its balance sheet, finance oil and gas operations and repay outstanding debts. The energy company said it would offer 4.08 billion ordinary shares at N50 each to existing shareholders on the basis of one new share for every two shares held. In a statement released on Friday, Oando said the rights issue had received regulatory approvals from the Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigerian Exchange Limited, Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the Financial Surveillance Department of the South African Reserve Bank. The company said proceeds from the offer, assuming full subscription, would be deployed to meet working capital requirements, finance capital expenditure on its Oil Mining Leases 60 to 63, repay debts and settle intra-group funding obligations. The capital raise comes after Oando acquired Nigerian Agip Oil Company in August 2024, a transaction that increased its participating interest in OMLs 60 to 63 from 20 per cent to 40 per cent and transferred operatorship of the assets to the company. Oando’s Group Chief Executive, Wale Tinubu, said the company needed a stronger capital structure to support its expanded asset base, finance new investments and improve cash generation. He said the funds would support balance sheet strengthening, working capital and the development of new oil and gas wells across the company’s upstream assets. The rights issue is also part of a recapitalisation programme authorised by shareholders at the company’s 46th Annual General Meeting held on 11c August, 2025. Shareholders had authorised the board to raise up to N500bn or its foreign currency equivalent. However, shareholders who fail to exercise their rights could see their percentage ownership diluted following the issuance of the additional shares. The company also said eligible investors could apply for additional shares beyond their entitlements, subject to allocation procedures and regulatory requirements. For shareholders on the Nigerian register, the acceptance list will open on 7 December, 2026, while trading in the rights on the NGX will also commence on that date. The offer will close on 15 January, 2027, with the listing of the new shares expected on 8 February, 2027, subject to regulatory clearance. Oando said shareholders recorded on its Nigerian register as of 13 February, 2026, would qualify for the offer. The company also outlined a separate timetable for shareholders on its South African register, with the rights issue opening on 7 December and closing on 15 January, 2027. The new shares will rank equally with the company’s existing ordinary shares once issued. Odinaka Anudu
